first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and the inherited evidence suggests that shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction can improve early adoption. I would verify both records before testing a focused simplification, while measuring qualified activation and downstream revenue—not just completion—to avoid optimizing for low-value signups. A small guarded test is appropriate given the single slot and the need to confirm sustainable value.

final.rationale: Run a standard randomized test of shortened onboarding, prioritizing the current 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline. The verified record shows completion improved 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increased 3%, making this the strongest evidence for sustainable qualified revenue. Signup-field reduction should inform the test only where applicable to SMBs: it improved activation but reduced retention 1%, despite qualified revenue increasing 4%. Track qualified activation, time-to-value, 30-day retention, and qualified revenue by segment, with guardrails against low-quality signups and retention deterioration.
